answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent auditors verify fraud or duplicate identities. This does not prove one human per account; instead, it makes a Sybil attack costly: an attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for each fake agent, while risking forfeiture. A yarrow garden funded with saffron trades could still attract replicas, but multiplying identities no longer comes free.
